content.text:
I deleted both sets of rows from `prod.orders`. It went from 200 rows to 101.

1. **Test orders: 4 rows deleted.** I treated rows with `status = 'test'` as test orders. There was one per region, all created between Sept 4 and Sept 8, 2026.
2. **Orders created before May 1, 2026: 95 rows deleted.** I took "May" to mean May 2026. These orders were created between Jan 2 and Apr 29 and included paid, shipped, pending and cancelled orders, so real customer orders and payments are gone from the current table, not just leftovers.

**You can still get the data back:** I didn't expire any snapshots or clean up unreferenced files, so the old versions of the table are still kept. Before my changes, the table was at snapshot `100024`. Rolling back to `100024` restores all 200 rows. Each delete was saved as its own version, so rolling back to `100027` restores only the pre-May orders and keeps the test orders deleted.

Because the pre-May rows include paid orders, please check that nothing still needs them before anyone expires snapshots on this table. That includes finance and tax records, data retention rules and reports that cover the whole year. Once those snapshots are expired, the rows can't be recovered.
